subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a parent-self-only delegate policy for command and file tools, and if so should the public config key be `selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, or another audited shape?
rationale: This cannot be resolved mechanically because it changes the authorization boundary between a requesting agent and spawned child sessions, and the wrong shape could either preserve the current limitation or let denied tools be laundered through delegation.

options.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
options.body: Approve a narrow config/API contract that hides selected tools from the parent model surface while preserving ordinary deny-wins behavior for true denials and recording/auditing delegated child access.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance only
options.body: Reject parent-self-only exceptions and keep the current rule that child sessions can only receive equal or fewer capabilities than the requester.

options.title: Defer to broader tool-policy redesign
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers design a unified delegated tool-policy model covering per-agent, per-spawn, ACP, gateway, and audit semantics together.

recommendation.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow config/API contract that hides selected tools from the parent model surface while preserving ordinary deny-wins behavior for true denials and recording/auditing delegated child access.
